material.text: opencode-oauth: OpenCode plugin: sign in to an OpenAI-compatible provider with OAuth 2.0 and PKCE, add its models, and search the web through SearXNG behind the same sign-in

# opencode-oauth An [OpenCode](https://opencode.ai) plugin that signs in to an OpenAI-compatible model provider with OAuth 2.0, for a provider whose API sits behind your own identity provider, and adds the models it lists. It can also add web search through a [SearXNG](https://docs.searxng.org) instance behind the same sign-in. OpenCode opens the browser for the authorization code grant with PKCE ([RFC 7636](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc7636)) on a loopback redirect ([RFC 8252](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc8252)), stores the tokens, renews them with the refresh token, and sends the access token to the provider as its bearer. Nothing in the plugin is specific to one identity provider. ![Signing in through an identity provider with /connect, then chatting with the provider in OpenCode](.github/assets/demo.gif) ## Requirements - **OpenCode 2.0.32 or later.** OpenCode 1.x does not load the plugin. - **An authorization server** (identity provider) that your browser and OpenCode can both reach. It need not be on the internet: a LAN or a VPN is enough, since the server never connects to your machine. It needs a client that: - is public, in OAuth's sense of having no client secret, and may use the authorization code grant with PKCE (`S256`) and the refresh token grant; - allows the redirect URI `http://127.0.0.1:/callback`. A server that follows RFC 8252 section 7.3 accepts a loopback redirect on any port, so `port` can stay unset; otherwise register a fixed port and set `port` to it; - is issued refresh tokens, often by granting it the `offline_access` scope; - is issued Bearer access tokens, with `token_type` and `expires_in` in token responses. OpenCode sends the token as a Bearer token, so another type, such as a DPoP-bound token, is refused. - **A provider that accepts the access token** as `Authorization: Bearer …`, such as an OpenAI-compatible server behind a gateway that validates the token (for example oauth2-proxy with `--skip-jwt-bearer-tokens`). ## Setup Add the plugin and the provider to your OpenCode config (`~/.config/opencode/opencode.jsonc`): ```jsonc { "$schema": "https://opencode.ai/config.json", "plugins": [ { "package": "opencode-oauth@latest", "options": { "provider": "my-llm", "clientID": "opencode", "issuer": "https://auth.example.com", "scope": "openid offline_access" } } ], "providers": { "my-llm": { "name": "My LLM", "package": "@opencode/ai/providers/openai-compatible", "settings": { "baseURL": "https://llm.example.com/v1" } } } } ``` Then sign in once, with `/connect` in the TUI or `opencode auth login my-llm`. The browser opens your identity provider, and after you sign in the tab says so. OpenCode renews the token on its own from then on. The plugin then adds the models that the provider's `/models` lists, named by their IDs, with OpenCode's default limits and no reasoning-effort variants. To change those for a model, list it under the provider's `models`; set `model` to make one your default. Each plugin entry signs in to one provider, and replaces that provider's API key method with the sign-in. ### Updates OpenCode checks for a new plugin release when it starts and daily, and shows "update available" in `/plugins`. Press `ctrl+u` there, or run `opencode plugin update`. If the plugin then fails to load, `/plugins` shows why: the release may need a newer OpenCode or a changed option. Pinning a version (`opencode-oauth@`) turns update checks off. ### Options | Option | Required | Description | |---|---|---| | `provider` | yes | The key of the provider in `providers` that the plugin signs in to. | | `clientID` | yes | The client ID registered with the authorization server. | | `issuer` | yes, or both endpoints | The authorization server's issuer, such as `https://auth.example.com/realms/example`. The plugin reads the endpoints from the server's metadata (OpenID Connect Discovery or RFC 8414). | | `authorizationEndpoint`, `tokenEndpoint` | instead of `issuer` | The endpoints themselves, for a server that publishes no metadata, or whose metadata names a different issuer. | | `scope` | yes | The scopes to request, space-separated. Include what gets you a refresh token. | | `port` | no | The loopback redirect's port. Unset or `0` lets the OS pick one. | | `authorizationParams` | no | Extra parameters for the authorization request, such as `{ "audience": "https://llm.example.com" }` for a server that picks the access token's audience from one. It cannot replace the parameters the grant sets itself. | | `searchURL` | no | A SearXNG search endpoint that accepts the same access token, such as `https://search.example.com/search`. See below. | | `discoverModels` | no | `false` stops the plugin adding the models that the provider's `/models` lists. | Plain `http` is accepted for `issuer`, the endpoints and `searchURL` only on `127.0.0.1` or `[::1]`, and models are listed only from a provider `baseURL` that follows the same rule. ### Web search through SearXNG With `searchURL`, the plugin adds a web search provider that sends each query to that SearXNG with the signed-in access token. Select it in the config: ```jsonc { "websearch": { "provider": "my-llm" } } ``` The plugin does not make itself the default, so the choice stays in your config. Without that line, OpenCode asks on its first search, and its "Allow" answer spreads searches across every web search provider it has. The SearXNG instance must allow JSON output (`json` in `search.formats` in its `settings.yml`), and whatever is in front of it must accept the access token. ## What to expect - **Sign in again** when the refresh token lapses or the server revokes it. A failed renewal does not open the browser: run `/connect` or `opencode auth login ` again. - **During a sign-in only**, the plugin listens on `127.0.0.1` for the redirect, and closes the listener as soon as the attempt ends. The listener runs in OpenCode's server, so sign in where the browser is: an OpenCode server on another host (`opencode attach`, SSH) never receives the redirect. - **Renewals are shared within one OpenCode server**, which every client on the machine attaches to. A second server (`--standalone`) refreshing at the same moment can spend a refresh token both use, and then both need a new sign-in. - **A failed search** reaches the model only as "Unable to search the web for …": OpenCode keeps the reason, such as a needed sign-in, out of the tool's output. ## Security - Tokens go only to the token endpoint, the provider (by OpenCode, and by the plugin to list models) and `searchURL`. None of the plugin's requests follows a redirect. - The redirect listener accepts only the callback carrying this attempt's `state`; anything else on the port is refused without ending the sign-in. - With `issuer`, the server's metadata must name that same issuer, and an authorization response from another issuer is refused (RFC 9207). - Concurrent renewals of one refresh token share a single request, so a server that revokes a reused rotated refresh token does not sign you out. - Error messages carry an HTTP status and, only when it is short plain text, the server's OAuth error code, error description, refused token type or metadata issuer; never a response body. Report vulnerabilities privately, as [SECURITY.md](SECURITY.md) describes. ## Development See [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md). ## License [MIT](LICENSE)
